direct_question:
Audit the CURRENT refactored intake for completeness, not just documents. Can we make an accurate eligibility screening conclusion from these answers? List all missing facts, conditional visibility failures, precision gaps, program-specific eligibility-unit inputs, and mandatory unresolved criteria. Include concise simple followup wording and exactly when to ask it. Separate criteria facts from application paperwork.
What external documents would possibly be needed, and what rules/triggers necessitate them? Give a concrete document-to-question matrix for your program. Show questions already in our intake, questions needing further detail, and questions belonging in the actual application session. Assess whether our intake supports accurate preliminary eligibility conclusions. Retrieve official sources before answering.

mappings.question: Does [recipient name] own a primary residence, other real property, savings or investments, and what are current values and ownership details (sole, joint, trust)?
mappings.subject_and_period: Current ownership and values; date acquired; ownership form (sole/joint/trust).
mappings.proposed_followup_question: Please list each asset the recipient owns (primary home with address, other real estate with address, bank/account/investment type) and give an approximate current value and date of acquisition for each. Note joint owners and whether any property is held in a trust.
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: County must evaluate real and personal property values when determining Medi‑Cal eligibility; applicants may be denied for failure to provide required proof of asset values.
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: Any application or potential eligibility screening for Medi‑Cal long‑term services, waivers, or institutional Medi‑Cal; flagged when recipient.assets indicates property or savings.
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: If self‑reported values approach program asset limits, if recipient is institutionalized or applying for Medi‑Cal LTC, or if county requests proof; or if applicant reports 'I'm not sure'.
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Yes for a rough screening and to triage risk if values are clearly far below or far above likely thresholds; No for a defensible eligibility conclusion if values are near limits or transfers are possible.
alternatives: Page‑or‑account summaries, property tax bill, deed, escrow statement, brokerage statement (application/agency verification)
mappings.requirement_support: MEPM-ARTICLE-9 describes property verification and the need to provide proof of real/personal property; ACWDL-25-14 shows denial/discontinuance can occur for failure to provide proof of assets.
mappings.retrieval_support: MEPM-ARTICLE-9 (property verification rules), ACWDL-25-14 (notice/denial for failure to provide proof)
mappings.effective_date_or_jurisdiction_notes: California Department of Health Care Services (Medi‑Cal) rules; county will request documentation per MEPM.
mappings.review_notes: Intake asks only asset types (recipient.assets) without values, ownership form, dates, or estimated amounts. That prevents a defensible LTC/waiver eligibility decision.

mappings.question: Has the recipient given away or transferred money or property within the last 30 months? If yes: describe what, value, date, and recipient of transfer.
mappings.subject_and_period: Transfers/gifts within 30 months prior to institutional Medi‑Cal application.
mappings.proposed_followup_question: If yes, for each transfer provide: what was transferred, approximate value, date (mm/dd/yyyy), and to whom (name and relationship). If unsure, say 'unsure' and whether you have any supporting documents (deed, canceled checks, trust instruments).
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: Transfers within the lookback period may create a penalty period (period of ineligibility). The county must review transfers; failure to disclose/document can cause application denial.
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: Recipient is institutionalized or applying for nursing‑facility Medi‑Cal (recipient.living_setting = nursing home or skilled nursing facility).
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: If transfers reported or 'I'm not sure' selected, or if assets appear to have been reduced shortly before application.
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Self‑report can flag potential penalty exposure, but is NOT sufficient for a defensible eligibility calculation of penalty period length — agency review and documents required.
alternatives: Deeds, canceled checks, trust documents, statements of sale/gift, probate/trust reports (agency verification)
mappings.requirement_support: MEPM-ARTICLE-9 explains property and transfer verification procedures and the lookback implications for Medi‑Cal institutional eligibility.
mappings.review_notes: Intake only asks Yes/No/Unsure; it does not gather transfer descriptions, dates, or values required to estimate penalty periods.

mappings.program_or_pathway: HCBS waivers / AL waiver / DDS waiver (Medi‑Cal waivers)
mappings.question: Is there a certifying clinician or medical documentation that can attest to the recipient's need for services (functional limitation / medical necessity)?
mappings.subject_and_period: Current medical documentation or clinician able to produce an assessment for waiver eligibility or nursing‑facility discharge planning.
mappings.proposed_followup_question: Provide the certifying clinician's name, clinic, phone, date of last visit, and whether a written functional assessment (physician's statement, DHS form, home health or IHSS assessment) is available or can be obtained.
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: Waivers require medical/functional eligibility determinations and county referrals; some waivers ignore parental income or apply spousal impoverishment rules; county must receive waiver documentation and determine Medi‑Cal eligibility.
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: Applicant seeks waiver services, or recipient is institutionalized and may be referred for waiver-based Medi‑Cal; recipient.adl_needs indicates need for assistance.
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: If medical documentation is required for waiver admission or to support IHSS, county will request clinician's assessment, DHS waiver forms, or functional assessment.
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Yes to indicate potential medical eligibility and to triage to county waiver contact; No for final eligibility — county medical determination and formal documentation required.
alternatives: Physician statement, DHS 7071 or equivalent waiver forms, home health assessments, IHSS assessment (application/agency follows)
mappings.requirement_support: MEPM-ARTICLE-19 describes waiver referral process and that county will determine Medi‑Cal eligibility based on medical/functional evidence.
mappings.effective_date_or_jurisdiction_notes: California Medi‑Cal waiver procedures and county role.
mappings.review_notes: Intake captures whether conditions are documented and whether a clinician exists but lacks clinician contact details, dates, or the form/type of documentation — needed for a defensible medical eligibility claim.

mappings.program_or_pathway: Medi‑Cal asset verification and notice process
mappings.question: Can the recipient provide verifiable proof of asset values (bank statements, deeds, insurance summaries) when requested?
mappings.subject_and_period: Documentation covering current asset balances and recent history as requested by county during application/renewal.
mappings.proposed_followup_question: If asked by the county, can you obtain written proof of property values or account balances (e.g., recent bank or brokerage statements, property tax or deed)? If not, which documents are missing?
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: County may deny or discontinue Medi‑Cal for failure to provide required proof of assets; applicants must produce documentation when requested.
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: County requests proof or the intake indicates missing documents as an application barrier.
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: If applicant indicates 'Missing documents' in case.application_barriers or if the county issues a request for proof.
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Self‑report sufficient to note barriers but not sufficient for county approval; county will require originals or certified copies.
alternatives: Official asset proofs: bank statements, property deeds, insurance settlement letters (application)
mappings.requirement_support: ACWDL 25‑14 shows county notices and denials for failure to provide proof of assets.
mappings.effective_date_or_jurisdiction_notes: California county verification and notice rules for Medi‑Cal asset verification.
mappings.review_notes: Intake flags 'Missing documents' in case.application_barriers but does not map which documents are missing; intake should collect which asset proofs exist.

mappings.document_name: MEPM Article 19 — Special Services (waiver county contact & spousal impoverishment)
mappings.program_or_pathway: Waiver pathways with special eligibility rules (e.g., AL Waiver, DDS Waiver)
mappings.question: Is the recipient married? If yes, what are the spouse's living situation, income and asset details (so spousal impoverishment rules can be applied)?
mappings.subject_and_period: Current spouse status, residence, income and assets at application time.
mappings.proposed_followup_question: If married/partnered, provide spouse's name, whether spouse lives at home, spouse's monthly income types and approximate amounts, and whether spouse owns property or accounts jointly with the recipient.
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: Some waivers use special deeming/spousal impoverishment rules; county referral is required and spousal information is used to apply those rules.
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: Recipient indicates married/registered domestic partner or waiver pathway is being sought.
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: If married, county will require marriage certificate, spouse's proof of income and asset documentation to apply spousal impoverishment protections.
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Self‑report sufficient for initial triage; not sufficient for final spousal impoverishment calculation.
alternatives: Marriage certificate, spouse paystubs, SSA letters, bank statements (application)
mappings.requirement_support: MEPM‑ARTICLE‑19 describes waiver rules and that counties apply spousal impoverishment rules for certain waivers.
mappings.effective_date_or_jurisdiction_notes: California waiver-specific eligibility rules processed by county waiver contacts.
mappings.review_notes: Intake records marital status and spouse living situation but omits spouse income/asset amounts and ownership details needed for spousal calculations.

mappings.document_name: MEPM Article 19 — Special Services (county referral, program status)
mappings.program_or_pathway: Medi‑Cal / Waiver eligibility — proof of current Medi‑Cal enrollment, case number, and notices
mappings.question: Is the recipient currently enrolled in Medi‑Cal (BIC/case number) or has an active application/denial notice? Provide dates and case number if available.
mappings.subject_and_period: Current or recent Medi‑Cal status, last decision or application date (case control).
mappings.proposed_followup_question: If the recipient is enrolled or has a case, enter the county case number or Benefits Identification Card (BIC) number and the effective dates or last decision date. If there is an adverse notice, upload or state the notice date and the appeal/deadline date.
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: County will use existing Medi‑Cal case details, BIC, and notices to determine eligibility and deadlines for appeals; waiver referrals use county contacts.
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: Any self‑report of current enrollment or prior application/denial; especially if applicant reports adverse notice or pending application.
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: County will request benefit letters, approval/denial notices, or BIC for verification and to track deadlines.
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Self‑report is sufficient to triage and prioritize urgent deadlines; however, exact case numbers/documents are required for agency followup and appeals.
alternatives: Benefit letter, BIC, county notice, denial/approval letters (application/agency)
mappings.requirement_support: MEPM-ARTICLE-19 outlines county role and referral; ACWDL-25-14 shows notices for failure to provide documentation.
mappings.effective_date_or_jurisdiction_notes: California Medi‑Cal county-managed benefits and notices.
mappings.review_notes: Intake collects general program status but not case/BIC numbers or copies of notices — needed for precise appeals or to avoid missed deadlines.

mappings.document_name: MEPM Article 19 — Special Services (institutional timelines & facility info)
mappings.program_or_pathway: Institutional Medi‑Cal / discharge planning / waiver referral
mappings.question: What is the facility admission date, expected length of stay or discharge date, and facility name/address?
mappings.subject_and_period: Exact facility admission date and any planned discharge within 7/30/90 days.
mappings.proposed_followup_question: Enter facility name, admission date (mm/dd/yyyy), and whether a discharge is planned (and date). If discharge is imminent, note the planned residence after discharge.
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: Some waiver/eligibility processes may be initiated while the applicant is institutionalized; county waiver contact will coordinate eligibility while in facility.
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: If living_setting indicates hospital, nursing home, rehab, or group home and move_timeline indicates imminent discharge.
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: Facility admission records, discharge summaries, facility paperwork will be requested by county for institutional Medi‑Cal eligibility or waiver referral.
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Self‑report of dates is sufficient to triage urgency; agency will require facility records for formal processing.
alternatives: Facility admission forms, discharge summaries, hospital records (agency followup)
mappings.requirement_support: MEPM‑ARTICLE‑19 discusses county waivers and eligibility initiation while institutionalized and the need to coordinate with county waiver contacts.
mappings.effective_date_or_jurisdiction_notes: California county waiver referral and institutional processing.
mappings.review_notes: Intake captures general timeframe categories but not exact admission/discharge dates or facility identity needed for county processing and penalty/start date calculations.

missing_eligibility_questions: Citizenship / immigration / lawful presence status of the recipient (required for Medi‑Cal eligibility in many categories) — add: 'Is the recipient a U.S. citizen, a lawfully present immigrant, or other/unknown? If not a citizen, what is their immigration status and date of entry?' (application stage will require documents).
Exact asset values, dates of acquisition, ownership form, and whether assets are jointly owned or in trust (recipient.assets currently only captures types).
Full transfer history details for any transfers within the lookback period (dates, values, recipients, documentation) rather than only a 30‑month yes/no flag.
Spouse/partner income and assets breakdown when recipient is married (needed to apply spousal impoverishment rules): spouse name, monthly incomes, asset types and approximate values.
Specific identification of Medi‑Cal case or BIC, county case number, and dates of recent decisions or notices (case.control data).
Exact facility admission date (mm/dd/yyyy) when institutionalized (not just categorical length of stay) to compute eligibility and penalty/timelines.
Clarify the eligibility unit / who should be counted in Medi‑Cal determination (names and relationships of household members, ages) — intake only asks household_size number, not detailed composition.
Whether the recipient has an active power of attorney or legal representative and contact information (relevant for signatures and outreach during application).
result.intake_sufficiency_assessment: The current intake collects many high‑level facts useful for triage (addresses, living setting, ADL needs, rough income band, asset types, program statuses, whether conditions are documented). However it does NOT collect the precise facts required to make a defensible preliminary eligibility determination for Medi‑Cal institutional or waiver pathways: missing are precise asset values and ownership details, transfer descriptions/dates, immigration/citizenship status, spouse income/asset details, exact facility admission dates, and clinician contact/document specifics. For routine non‑LTC MAGI Medi‑Cal screening the intake may be adequate to flag likely eligibility, but for long‑term‑care, waiver, or nursing‑home Medi‑Cal pathways the intake lacks the precision and mandatory application facts needed for a defensible conclusion. Many documentary requirements are application/agency followup, but the intake should capture the missing facts that trigger those followups.
coverage_gaps: No question about recipient citizenship/lawful presence (critical for eligibility determination).

Asset questions only record presence/type (recipient.assets) not values, acquisition dates, ownership form, or account specifics — prevents preliminary calculation of asset compliance or likely share of cost.
Transfer lookback is a single yes/no/unsure without details (value, date, recipient) — can't estimate penalty period.
Spouse information insufficient (no spouse income/asset amounts) to apply spousal impoverishment rules.
Medical documentation and clinician contact details are not captured (only whether documented/has clinician) — prevents assessing whether medical evidence exists for waiver/waiver referrals.
Household composition lacks roster (names, ages, relationships) needed to determine Medi‑Cal eligibility unit vs household for income counting.
No intake capture of case/BIC numbers, benefit letters, or adverse notice copies/dates to reliably triage deadlines (intake captures that a notice exists but not its content or dates).

Identity and residency documentary requirements are not shown in retrieved sources and the intake does not prompt whether the user has acceptable forms of ID or residency proof — a visibility gap for application readiness.

Program (MSSP), and Department of Developmental Services (DDS) waivers (as described later in 
these procedures) disregard parental income and resources and also apply spousal impoverishment 
provisions, the IHSS-residual program does not. Therefore, a beneficiary who is ineligible for the 
IHSS-residual program solely because the IHSS-residual program counted parental income and 
resources or did not apply the spousal impoverishment provisions can receive PCSP if otherwise 
eligible. 
II. OVERVIEW 
If the applicant is in a waiver that uses special eligibility rules and helshe has been determined 
medically eligible or potentially medically eligible for a particular waiver, the agency responsible for 
the waiver will refer the applicant to the county contact for a Medi-Cal determination if helshe is not 
already receiving Medi-Cal with no monthly share of cost. Depending on the circumstances, this 
determination may be initiated while the applicant is still institutionalized or in a living arrangement 
different from the setting covered by the waiver. 
Those persons who are applying for waivers that do not follow special eligibility rules, ( Acquired 
Immune Deficiency Syndrome Waiver) or persons who do not or would not have excess property or a 
monthly share of cost using regular Medi-Cal rules will not

TE: Some people may not lose 
Medi-Cal, may not have a share of cost or will continue on SSI and SSI-based Medi- 
cal upon returning home because the family incomelproperty is below the Medi-cal 
or SSI limit. Persons who continue to be or are eligible for SSI or qualify for a zero 
SOC Medi-Cal because the family incomelproperty is below the limit do not need to 
be determined using special eligibility rules for the HCBS, MSSP, or DDS waivers. 
B. County Contact 
Each county shall designate a waiver contact person. The county waiver contact person will 
receive the request for a Medi-Cal eligibility determination from the referring agency, 
coordinate the Medi-Cal eligibility determination, and answer questions about the program 
even though the actual determination may be made by other county staff. The contact for 
each county is attached to these procedures. It is important that applicants be directed to 
the county contacts because they understand how to process those waivers that disregard 
parental income and resources and apply spousal impoverishment rules. Once the county 
receives a referral, the county will determine Medi-Cal eligibility based on the criteria for the 
appropriate waiver including the living arrangement covered by the waiver. 
I

There are four types of waivers that are discussed in these Procedures. The first three may have 
speci
